newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch closing debt market report.
newsitem.headline: Dutch closing debt market report.

text.p: Dutch bonds ended higher, spurred by heavy buying power and higher Bund futures.
Dealers said turnover was brisk, especially in guilder bonds maturing after 2004.
They said turnover came from all sides - Dutch buyers, foreign buyers, end-investors and professional traders were all in the market.
Traders said they noticed heavy switching out of Dutch short bonds into Dutch and German bonds maturing after 2006.
"Volumes are gigantic, and it's nothing but buyers," said one dealer.
He added that a lack of players willing to sell drove prices higher.
Today's issue of three ten-year Siemens bonds denominated in guilders (500 million), marks (750 million) and French francs (2.5 billion) did not noticeably pressure the ten-year segment.
"Everybody all over the world knows Siemens, the thing just sold like hot cakes," one dealer said.
The Dutch ten-year benchmark closed 35 basis points higher.
Spiralling Bund futures also contributed to the Dutch market's rise.
Dutch bonds halted their surge in the afternoon, as the German March Bund future failed to remain above its newly set record high of 103.02.
"But the undelying mood is good. I think we're heading for another rise," one dealer said.
